real_estate.homebuilder: Mortgage rates paused at 7.43%, just off Thursday's 52 week high, as sellers start trimming prices.
real_estate.commentary:
Rates finally took a breather. Mortgage News Daily has the 30-year at 7.43% today, down 0.02, and the 15-year unchanged at 7.10%. Thursday's 7.45% was the top of the 52 week range. The newsletter printed 7.45% and 7.10%, which were Thursday's readings.

Sellers are starting to respond. The newsletter's lead is price cuts multiplying as rates climb, and today's MLS export shows 95 listings across our 15 city table with a price change status, 22 of them in Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. The 10-Year closed Friday at 5.17%, a hair under Thursday's 5.18%, the highest close since 2007, so the pressure has not lifted.

Here is what that means on a real Fremont home. At today's median on market list price of $1,199,000, with 20% down, the loan is $959,200, which is high balance conforming here, not jumbo. Principal and interest is $6,661 a month at 7.43%, against $5,745 at 5.99%, the 52 week low. That is $916 more every month for the same house.

• Board wide: 2,788 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 172 coming soon and 229 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 714 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 629 are on the market and 85 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 257 live, 201 active, 36 coming soon, 20 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,199,000 at $781 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 28 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 183, Milpitas 117, Newark 91, Union City 66.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,089,000 at $675 a square foot. 291 homes are priced under a million, and 158 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

What this means for you: supply rose to 714 from 707 and the homes past 60 days fell to 158 from 166, so buyers are still writing offers at 7% rates. Buyers: ask your lender to price the 30-year FHA at 7.15% and a 7/6 ARM at 6.85% against the 7.43% fixed, and watch for price changes, because some sellers are adjusting. Sellers: the same house costs a buyer about $900 more a month than it did at the 52 week low, so price to this week's rate and get the first price right, rather than chasing the market down.

stocks.note: Levels are Friday, September 25 at the closing bell.
stocks.news:
Stocks finished the week higher even with the 10-Year near 5.2%. The S&P rose 0.51% Friday and 1.21% on the week, the Nasdaq gained 2.06% for the week, and the Dow's 0.93% Friday rally ended a three week losing streak.

Darden is the chart. LongHorn Steakhouse grew same-restaurant sales 6.2% last quarter, while Olive Garden, Darden's biggest brand at $1.33 billion in quarterly sales, managed 1.1%. The results came in just shy of Wall Street's estimates, and the stock fell 3.02% Thursday and another 3.61% Friday to $199.75. Record beef prices, apparently, have not kept anyone out of the steakhouse.

feature_image.alt: Horizontal bar chart of Darden same-restaurant sales growth in the first quarter of fiscal 2027: LongHorn Steakhouse 6.2%, other brands 3.8%, Darden overall 3.1%, Fine Dining 1.6%, Olive Garden 1.1%. Quarterly sales: LongHorn $861 million, other brands $705 million, Darden $3.20 billion, Fine Dining $304 million, Olive Garden $1.33 billion.
feature_image.caption: LongHorn led Darden's first quarter with same-restaurant sales up 6.2%, while Olive Garden, its largest brand, grew 1.1%. Every bar matches Darden's filing.
feature_image.source: Source: Darden Restaurants fiscal 2027 first quarter results, SEC Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1, September 24, 2026.

economy.note: The 10-Year, gold and silver are Friday, September 25: the Treasury daily yield curve close and the COMEX front month settlements against Thursday's. Brent is Thursday's settlement of the ICE November contract, the front month.
economy.commentary:
Layoffs are still rare. First time jobless claims fell to 197,000 in the week ending September 19, down 1,000, and the 4-week average slipped to 202,250, its lowest since early August. The same week a year ago was 219,000. Closer to home, California logged 34,931 claims, 6.6% fewer than the same week of 2025.

The 10-Year closed Friday at 5.17%, down 0.01, after Thursday's 5.18%, the highest close since 2007. The newsletter printed 5.19% and up 0.03 for Thursday; the Treasury curve says 5.18% and up 0.07. Gold settled up 0.54% at $4,321.20 and silver up 1.25% at $64.80.

The Brent card is Thursday's settlement, $106.60, up 3.41%; the newsletter had $105.97 and down 0.58%. Friday it gave back 2.14% to settle at $104.32, on hopes that shipping through the Strait of Hormuz could reopen.

feature_image.alt: Line chart of U.S. weekly initial jobless claims, seasonally adjusted, for every week of 2026 through September 19, with the 4-week average. Claims ranged from a low of 189,000 in July to highs of 230,000 in January and June, and ended at 197,000, with the 4-week average at 202,000, below a dashed line at 219,000 marking the same week last year.
feature_image.caption: Weekly claims are at 197,000 and the 4-week average at 202,250, both below the 219,000 of the same week last year. California's own count fell 6.6% from a year earlier.
feature_image.source: Source: U.S. Department of Labor weekly claims via FRED (ICSA, IC4WSA, CAICLAIMS), week ending September 19, 2026.
